title: Customer IaC hooks, module composition, and safe upgrade guards for Private deployments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a repeatable, customer-specific IaC composition pattern for Private (VPC) deployments that supports per-customer variable overrides, extension modules, and a CI-driven pre/post upgrade hook system with built-in safety guards and health checks. Goal: enable customers to safely take minor/major runtime and infra upgrades with deterministic rollback paths and measurable health gating. This ticket defines the developer-facing module layout, the variable schema, the CI hook contract, and the runtime health-check suite used by the upgrade pipeline.
background_and_problem_statement: Customers want to customize networking, ingress, and monitoring wiring for Private deployments while still getting safe automated upgrades from Redwood. Current approaches (ad-hoc per-customer tfstate forks or unmanaged local patches) increase upgrade toil and break assumptions in the runtime. We need a composable pattern that keeps the base module authoritative while allowing extensions and per-customer small overlays without fragmenting the upgrade surface.
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce a three-layer composition: 1) redwood/core modules (reference implementations), 2) redwood/ext modules for optional integrations (KMS, private registry, CNIs), 3) customer wrappers that import core+ext and provide a thin variable override file and well-defined hook points executed by the CI pipeline. Hooks are not Terraform-native; they are realized by the CI runner and short-lived tasks (pre-apply validations, post-apply smoke-tests, and rollback validators). Upgrade safety is enforced via plan analysis, canary targets, and measured health gates (synthetic checks + metric thresholds).
module_layout_and_naming: Pattern: modules/core/<component> (stateful canonical resources), modules/ext/<integration> (optional modules designed to be composable), tenants/<customer_id>/main.tf (tenant wrapper module that calls core + ext and supplies tenant.tfvars). Naming convention: redwood_core_* for base resources, redwood_ext_* for extension resources, redwood_customer_<id>_* for tenant-scoped resources. Keep provider blocks in tenant wrappers so customers can pin region/account-level settings.
variable_schema_and_validation: Expose a small public surface on core modules. Complex customization is handled by ext modules to avoid combinatorial explosion. Use typed variables and validation blocks in Terraform (validation { condition = ... message = ... }) for common errors (CIDR overlaps, missing KMS keys, incompatible machine types). Encourage use of maps for feature flags and lists for ordered CIDR blocks. Document required/optional vars in a single tenants/<customer>/README.md and generate JSON schema for automated validation in CI.
extension_points_and_safe_customization_: Do not allow customers to directly replace critical stateful resources (control-plane secrets, primary storage). Provide extension modules for network hooks (eg. custom route tables), ingress controllers, and monitoring agents. Extension modules must declare a compatible interface (inputs/outputs) and pass a compatibility test during CI (terraform plan + provider version check). Any extension that requires a replacement of a core resource must be gated behind a manual review label in the pipeline.
upgrade_strategy_and_hooks: Upgrade pipeline stages: 1) pre-check (static validation of tfvars + schema), 2) dry-run plan capture and automated plan diff analysis (fail on resource deletes of protected types), 3) pre-upgrade hook: snapshot relevant state (S3 lock copy) and run pre-flight integration tests (connectivity, KMS access), 4) apply canary (a subset of tenant resources or a single zone namespace), 5) post-apply health gate: run smoke tests, check metrics (latency/error budgets), verify KV cache integrity, 6) full rollout or rollback based on gate. Hooks are implemented as CI jobs that invoke Terraform and then execute short-lived test runners (Go binaries or Python scripts) against endpoints created by the apply. Hook contract: hook scripts must emit structured JSON to artifacts for automatic parsing by the pipeline.
health_checks_and_metrics: Define a standardized smoke-test suite that runs after each apply: 1) API liveness probe (status endpoint), 2) short prompt end-to-end test (known prompt -> response validation), 3) background job status (queues/consumers), 4) prometheus/metric checks (token generation rate, error rate). Map health check results to Datadog/Prometheus dashboards and create templated monitors (alert if error rate > 1% for 5m after change). Post-apply health-check failures auto-trigger rollback jobs.
rollback_and_state_management: Always snapshot state before upgrades: create a named state backup and artifact link. Keep a rollback playbook that consists of: terraform apply using the last known-good tfstate (where possible), run post-rollback health checks, and escalate to oncall if rollback fails. For cases where resource replacement is destructive, the pipeline must mark the upgrade as manual and require an oncall approval step.
automation_and_ci_integration: Implementation in Terraform Cloud/Run/Orbs or GitHub Actions: pipeline YAML with explicit stages matching the upgrade strategy. Use plan artifact retention, automated plan analysis (we'll add a small CLI tool to detect deleting protected resources), and a hook runner service that executes pre/post hook scripts in sandboxed ephemeral runners. Ensure logs and artifacts are stored in our S3 bucket and linked in the Linear ticket via PRs.
acceptance_criteria: Reference module layout and tenant wrapper example committed to repo: infra/private-reference/tenants/example-corp
CI pipeline executes pre/post hooks and stores JSON artifacts for parsing
Automated plan analysis blocks any change that deletes protected control-plane resources
Post-upgrade health gate (smoke tests + metric checks) triggers rollback on failure
Documentation: tenants/README.md with variable schema and step-by-step upgrade runbook
implementation_notes: Start with network + console + runtime components as the initial core modules for composition
Build a small 'plan-analyzer' binary (Go) that rejects plans with resource deletions tagged protected=true
Use provider-level pinning in tenant wrappers to avoid accidental provider upgrades during sensitive changes
Keep extension modules in a separate registry path to enable independent CI testing
Add a test harness that can stand up a minimal tenant in our dev VPC for rapid preflight tests
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Too many per-customer customizations cause divergence. Mitigation: enforce extension modules and disallow direct core resource replacement.
Risk: Hooks introduce flakiness in CI. Mitigation: keep hooks short, idempotent, and provide retry/backoff with clear failure semantics.
Risk: State drift between environments. Mitigation: nightly drift detection job and scheduled reconciliation runs with alerts.
